prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; protects separation/authority/regulation. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) displays positions/routes/alarms/performance, proposes regulation, shows action/train/recovery before confirmation; sends Crew Login Token Bundle; non-vital only. Line Traffic Controller assesses passenger/downstream impacts, owns regulation, produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice (limits/speed/start/removal), monitors recovery, logs incident/time/train/location/passengers/first-safe-instruction. Voice Dispatch Console instructions require Revenue Train Operator readback; never replace safety validation. Operator reports condition/cab/passengers/local hazards. Maintenance Diagnostic Server supplies non-vital trends to Signal Maintenance Engineer, who advises recovery. Service Timetable Server changes require approved workflow/controller visibility verification. Passenger Information Gateway receives service state; distributes approved platform/destination messages. North District Zone Controller (Marble), South District Zone Controller (Orchid): respective districts/turnbacks/East-West approaches. Transfers require ownership/overlap/receiver-validation; restrictive evidence governs. East Junction Interlocking (Falcon), West Junction Interlocking retain locking; authorities require proved/locked points/protected overlaps/flanks; release requires detection/correspondence/opposing-route checks. Correspondence loss safely reduces authority. Axle counters independently prove availability; East sends Axle Counter Reset Request, prohibited with locked routes/approaches. Maple (full name unspecified) records clearance. West sends Route Release Exception List; hazards persist until exclusion. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot per face: closed/locked/bypassed/inhibited/faulted; not route proof. Safety-relevant platform state constrains arrival/dwell/departure; departure command requires direction-compatible doors; Marble suppresses unsafe-berth departure authority. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token, enforces profiles; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed/boundary-confidence; divergence increases uncertainty/separation. Reject stale acknowledgements. Train Radio Modem uses Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron), sends Radio Handover Audit File; degradation retains validated authority; loss may require holds. Safety Data Communication Network identified. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance checks certificate-validity/clock-tolerance using sample report; produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack during approved maintenance, records change-reference. Cyber Security Officer reviews

New part:
S133: Station status indications presented to local station staff are derived from validated CBTC states rather than from unverified field contacts alone.
S134: These indications distinguish normal service, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop active, and evacuation support conditions.
S135: The Metro Operations Control System displays station and platform states with the same identifiers used in controller workstations to reduce interpretation errors during incidents.
S136: Passenger Information Gateway receives train prediction data, stopping pattern changes, and platform allocation updates after the CBTC system has reconciled them with the active timetable.
S137: The Passenger Information Gateway shall not publish a revised destination or skip-stop message until the underlying train identity and route have been confirmed by the CBTC system.
S138: When a platform is taken out of service, the passenger information interface marks the affected train movements as unavailable for boarding while retaining their operational tracking in the control center.
S139: Service Timetable Server provides planned service context used to compare predicted arrivals against scheduled platform usage.
S140: Metro Operations Control System coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, and station crowding information before it is released to passenger-facing systems.
S141: Voice Dispatch Console displays train calling identity, current platform association, and the latest operational hold reason so that spoken instructions match automated indications.
S142: The Line Traffic Controller may apply a station hold through dispatch controls, and the hold is reflected in CBTC departure logic without changing the underlying route locking rules.
S143: Dispatch-related controls use positive confirmation and cancellation states so that a cancelled hold is not confused with a timeout, failed message, or rejected command.
S144: Kestrel shall report train door enable side, berth identity, and departure readiness to support platform interface checks during dwell and dispatch.
S145: Saffron shall maintain message delivery paths for station interface traffic during normal radio coverage transitions and degraded coverage recovery.
S146: Train Radio Modem uses the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before accepting renewed secure sessions for passenger-facing and station-interface data paths.
S147: Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-relevant station interface messages separately from nonvital passenger information messages.
S148: Maintenance Diagnostic Server records station interface faults, rejected commands, and inconsistent indications for later investigation by the Signal Maintenance Engineer.
S149: Cyber Security Officer reviews access rights for passenger information and dispatch integration workstations when station-facing interfaces are commissioned or materially changed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
